WORKPLACE VIOLENCE PREVENTION PLAN — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Jordan Alex Lee · Acme Corp

ABOUT THIS WORKPLACE VIOLENCE PREVENTION PLAN INFORMATION SHEET
This Workplace Violence Prevention Plan — Information Sheet describes California's requirement that most employers establish, implement, and maintain a written workplace violence prevention plan, set out in Labor Code § 6401.9 (added by SB 553 and operative, for most of its requirements, on and after July 1, 2024), as that requirement relates to the working relationship between Jordan Alex Lee and Acme Corp.

It summarizes selected requirements of that statute: which employers, employees, and places of employment the requirement covers and one example of a statutory exemption; the duty to have a written plan and how the plan may be maintained; selected elements the plan itself must contain, including identifying who is responsible for it, procedures for accepting and responding to reports of workplace violence without retaliation, and procedures for identifying, evaluating, and correcting workplace violence hazards; the training the statute requires; the violent incident log requirement; and recordkeeping, including employee access to certain records.

This corpus's separate Injury and Illness Prevention Program (IIPP) — Information Sheet describes a related but distinct statute, Labor Code § 6401.7, and its implementing regulation, 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 3203; that document's own "gap" disclosures note that it named § 6401.9 only as a topic § 6401.7 cross-references, without independently fetching or verifying § 6401.9's own text. This information sheet is the independent verification of § 6401.9 itself that the IIPP document deliberately deferred; it does not restate the IIPP document's content, and it does not independently verify 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 3203 beyond quoting the handful of places where § 6401.9's own text cross-references that regulation by section and subdivision number.

Acme Corp has identified Taylor Morgan as a person responsible for implementing its plan.

This information sheet is not itself Acme Corp's written workplace violence prevention plan, does not itself satisfy Labor Code § 6401.9's written-plan requirement, and does not determine that any particular practice of Acme Corp's is or is not compliant with California law.

WHICH EMPLOYERS AND WORKPLACES THE REQUIREMENT COVERS
Labor Code § 6401.9(b)(1) itself states the requirement's general reach: 'Except as provided in paragraph (2), this section applies to all employers, employees, places of employment, and employer-provided housing.' Paragraph (2) of subdivision (b) then lists categories of employers, employees, and places of employment that are exempt from the section, subject to the division's authority in paragraph (3) to order an otherwise-exempt employer to comply anyway. One example of a listed exemption, subdivision (b)(2)(E), exempts 'Employees teleworking from a location of the employee's choice, which is not under the control of the employer.' The statute lists five other exempt categories in subdivision (b)(2) — health care facilities and employers already covered by a separate Title 8 regulation on workplace violence in health care (Cal. Code Regs., tit. 8, § 3342), certain Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation facilities, certain law-enforcement agencies meeting POST compliance requirements, and small worksites with fewer than 10 employees that are not accessible to the public and that comply with 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 3203 — none of which are quoted or summarized further in this clause.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-02]
  "Except as provided in paragraph (2), this section applies to all employers, employees, places of employment, and employer-provided housing."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 6401.9 (California Legislative Information text), Lab. Code § 6401.9, subd. (b)(1) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=6401.9.)
  "Employees teleworking from a location of the employee’s choice, which is not under the control of the employer."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 6401.9 (California Legislative Information text), Lab. Code § 6401.9, subd. (b)(2)(E) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=6401.9.)
  Known gap: This clause quotes only the general applicability rule in subdivision (b)(1) and one of the six exemption categories listed in subdivision (b)(2), the teleworking exemption in subparagraph (E); it does not quote or fully summarize the other five exemption categories (health care facilities and employers subject to 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 3342, Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation facilities, qualifying law enforcement agencies, and small non-public worksites under 10 employees), each of which carries its own conditions in the statutory text. Both quotations in this clause are drawn from the same enacted statute, Labor Code § 6401.9 — subdivisions (b)(1) and (b)(2)(E) of one section — not independent sources from one another; this document's only independent source is § 6401.9 itself, fetched twice from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov using two distinct request methods and confirmed byte-identical (after whitespace normalization) before any of its text was treated as verified. This clause does not independently verify the separate regulation it names in passing, 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 3342 (the health-care-specific workplace violence prevention standard) or § 3203, beyond quoting § 6401.9's own cross-reference to their section numbers; no claim is made here about either regulation's content. This is a description of what one state's statute requires in general, not a determination that any particular employer, employee, or place of employment does or does not fall within an exemption.

THE DUTY TO HAVE A WRITTEN PLAN AND HOW IT MAY BE MAINTAINED
Labor Code § 6401.9(c)(1)(A) states the core duty in a single sentence: 'An employer shall establish, implement, and maintain an effective workplace violence prevention plan.' Subdivision (c)(1)(B) then adds three requirements about the plan's form and availability: it 'shall be in writing and shall be available and easily accessible to employees, authorized employee representatives, and representatives of the division at all times'; it 'shall be in effect at all times and in all work areas and be specific to the hazards and corrective measures for each work area and operation'; and — addressing how it relates to the separate Injury and Illness Prevention Program (IIPP) requirement of Labor Code § 6401.7 and 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 3203 — 'The written plan may be incorporated as a stand-alone section in the written injury and illness prevention program required by Section 3203 of Title 8 of the California Code of Regulations or maintained as a separate document.'

[Verified — checked 2026-09-02]
  "An employer shall establish, implement, and maintain an effective workplace violence prevention plan."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 6401.9 (California Legislative Information text), Lab. Code § 6401.9, subd. (c)(1)(A) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=6401.9.)
  "The plan shall be in writing and shall be available and easily accessible to employees, authorized employee representatives, and representatives of the division at all times."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 6401.9 (California Legislative Information text), Lab. Code § 6401.9, subd. (c)(1)(B) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=6401.9.)
  "The written plan may be incorporated as a stand-alone section in the written injury and illness prevention program required by Section 3203 of Title 8 of the California Code of Regulations or maintained as a separate document."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 6401.9 (California Legislative Information text), Lab. Code § 6401.9, subd. (c)(1)(B) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=6401.9.)
  Known gap: This clause corrects an assumption that a workplace violence prevention plan must always be a document separate from an employer's IIPP — the statutory text quoted here expressly allows the plan to be incorporated as a stand-alone section of the written IIPP instead. Both quotations are drawn from the same enacted statute, Labor Code § 6401.9 — subparagraphs (A) and (B) of a single paragraph, (c)(1) — not independent sources from one another; this document's only independent source is § 6401.9 itself, fetched twice from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov using two distinct request methods and confirmed byte-identical (after whitespace normalization) before any of its text was treated as verified. This clause does not independently verify the separate IIPP statute or regulation it names, Labor Code § 6401.7 or 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 3203; those are addressed, on their own terms, in this corpus's separate Injury and Illness Prevention Program (IIPP) — Information Sheet, and no claim about their content beyond the bare cross-reference is made here.

SELECTED ELEMENTS THE PLAN ITSELF MUST CONTAIN
Labor Code § 6401.9(c)(2) states that '[t]he plan shall include all of the following:' and then enumerates thirteen lettered elements, subparagraphs (A) through (M). This clause quotes a selection of those elements rather than all thirteen. Subparagraph (A) requires 'Names or job titles of the persons responsible for implementing the plan. If there are multiple persons responsible for the plan, their roles shall be clearly described.' Subparagraph (D) requires 'Effective procedures for the employer to accept and respond to reports of workplace violence, and to prohibit retaliation against an employee who makes such a report.' Subparagraph (I) requires 'Procedures to identify and evaluate workplace violence hazards, including, but not limited to, scheduled periodic inspections to identify unsafe conditions and work practices and employee reports and concerns. Inspections shall be conducted when the plan is first established, after each workplace violence incident, and whenever the employer is made aware of a new or previously unrecognized hazard.' Subparagraph (J) requires 'Procedures to correct workplace violence hazards identified and evaluated in subparagraph (I) in a timely manner consistent with paragraph (6) of subdivision (a) of Section 3203 of Title 8 of the California Code of Regulations.'

[Verified — checked 2026-09-02]
  "The plan shall include all of the following:"
  — Cal. Labor Code § 6401.9 (California Legislative Information text), Lab. Code § 6401.9, subd. (c)(2) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=6401.9.)
  "Names or job titles of the persons responsible for implementing the plan. If there are multiple persons responsible for the plan, their roles shall be clearly described."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 6401.9 (California Legislative Information text), Lab. Code § 6401.9, subd. (c)(2)(A) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=6401.9.)
  "Effective procedures for the employer to accept and respond to reports of workplace violence, and to prohibit retaliation against an employee who makes such a report."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 6401.9 (California Legislative Information text), Lab. Code § 6401.9, subd. (c)(2)(D) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=6401.9.)
  "Procedures to identify and evaluate workplace violence hazards, including, but not limited to, scheduled periodic inspections to identify unsafe conditions and work practices and employee reports and concerns. Inspections shall be conducted when the plan is first established, after each workplace violence incident, and whenever the employer is made aware of a new or previously unrecognized hazard."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 6401.9 (California Legislative Information text), Lab. Code § 6401.9, subd. (c)(2)(I) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=6401.9.)
  "Procedures to correct workplace violence hazards identified and evaluated in subparagraph (I) in a timely manner consistent with paragraph (6) of subdivision (a) of Section 3203 of Title 8 of the California Code of Regulations."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 6401.9 (California Legislative Information text), Lab. Code § 6401.9, subd. (c)(2)(J) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=6401.9.)
  Known gap: This clause quotes 4 of the 13 lettered elements the statute requires the plan to contain — subparagraphs (A), (D), (I), and (J). It does not quote or summarize the other 9 (employee-involvement procedures, multi-employer coordination, supervisory-compliance procedures, communication procedures, emergency-response procedures, training-development procedures, postincident-response and investigation procedures, plan-review procedures, and a catch-all for standards the division and standards board may later require); those are named in this document's introductory clause only as topics the statute covers, not summarized or quoted here, so as not to state anything about their specific content that has not been verified. All four quotations are drawn from the same enacted statute, Labor Code § 6401.9 — subparagraphs of a single paragraph, (c)(2) — not independent sources from one another; this document's only independent source is § 6401.9 itself, fetched twice from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov using two distinct request methods and confirmed byte-identical (after whitespace normalization) before any of its text was treated as verified. Subparagraph (J)'s cross-reference to 'paragraph (6) of subdivision (a) of Section 3203 of Title 8 of the California Code of Regulations' is quoted here only as § 6401.9's own text; this document does not independently verify what that regulatory paragraph itself says, and no claim is made about its content. This is a description of what the statute requires a plan to contain in general, not a claim about the content of any particular employer's actual plan.

WHEN EMPLOYEE TRAINING IS REQUIRED
Labor Code § 6401.9(e)(1) states the general training duty: 'The employer shall provide effective training to employees, as specified in paragraphs (2) and (3).' Subdivision (e)(2) then fixes the timing of the main round of training: 'The employer shall provide employees with initial training when the plan is first established, and annually thereafter, on all of the following:' — followed by six lettered topics the statute requires that training to cover, including the employer's plan itself, the definitions and requirements of the section, how to report incidents without fear of reprisal, and the job-specific hazards and corrective measures relevant to the employees being trained. Subdivision (e)(3) then adds a second, event-triggered training duty distinct from the annual cycle: 'Additional training shall be provided when a new or previously unrecognized workplace violence hazard has been identified and when changes are made to the plan. The additional training may be limited to addressing the new workplace violence hazard or changes to the plan.'

[Verified — checked 2026-09-02]
  "The employer shall provide effective training to employees, as specified in paragraphs (2) and (3)."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 6401.9 (California Legislative Information text), Lab. Code § 6401.9, subd. (e)(1) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=6401.9.)
  "The employer shall provide employees with initial training when the plan is first established, and annually thereafter, on all of the following:"
  — Cal. Labor Code § 6401.9 (California Legislative Information text), Lab. Code § 6401.9, subd. (e)(2) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=6401.9.)
  "Additional training shall be provided when a new or previously unrecognized workplace violence hazard has been identified and when changes are made to the plan. The additional training may be limited to addressing the new workplace violence hazard or changes to the plan."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 6401.9 (California Legislative Information text), Lab. Code § 6401.9, subd. (e)(3) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=6401.9.)
  Known gap: This clause quotes the introductory sentence of subdivision (e)(2) but does not quote or fully summarize all six lettered topics that paragraph requires the annual training to cover; only a general description of some of those topics is given in the body text above, not a verified quotation of each one. All three quotations in this clause are drawn from the same enacted statute, Labor Code § 6401.9 — paragraphs (1), (2), and (3) of a single subdivision, (e) — not independent sources from one another; this document's only independent source is § 6401.9 itself, fetched twice from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov using two distinct request methods and confirmed byte-identical (after whitespace normalization) before any of its text was treated as verified. This is a description of what the statute requires in general, not a claim about the content or timing of any training a particular employer has or has not provided to a particular employee.

THE VIOLENT INCIDENT LOG REQUIREMENT
Labor Code § 6401.9(d)(1)(A) states a duty distinct from the plan itself: 'The employer shall record information in a violent incident log for every workplace violence incident.' The statute separately protects the privacy of the people involved: subdivision (d)(1)(B) requires that 'The employer shall omit any element of personal identifying information sufficient to allow identification of any person involved in a violent incident, such as the person's name, address, electronic mail address, telephone number, social security number, or other information that, alone or in combination with other publicly available information, reveals the person's identity.' Subdivision (d)(2) then lists categories of information the log must include for each incident — such as the date, time, and location of the incident, the type of workplace violence involved, a description of the incident, and a classification of who committed it and the circumstances — which are not separately quoted in this clause.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-02]
  "The employer shall record information in a violent incident log for every workplace violence incident."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 6401.9 (California Legislative Information text), Lab. Code § 6401.9, subd. (d)(1)(A) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=6401.9.)
  "The employer shall omit any element of personal identifying information sufficient to allow identification of any person involved in a violent incident, such as the person’s name, address, electronic mail address, telephone number, social security number, or other information that, alone or in combination with other publicly available information, reveals the person’s identity."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 6401.9 (California Legislative Information text), Lab. Code § 6401.9, subd. (d)(1)(B) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=6401.9.)
  Known gap: This clause quotes the log's basic recording duty and its anonymization requirement, subparagraphs (A) and (B) of paragraph (1) of subdivision (d), but does not quote or fully summarize the itemized list of information categories in paragraph (2) of subdivision (d), nor the multiemployer-worksite provision in subparagraph (C) of paragraph (1). Both quotations are drawn from the same enacted statute, Labor Code § 6401.9 — subparagraphs of a single paragraph, (d)(1) — not independent sources from one another; this document's only independent source is § 6401.9 itself, fetched twice from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov using two distinct request methods and confirmed byte-identical (after whitespace normalization) before any of its text was treated as verified. This is a description of what the statute requires the log to contain and how identifying details must be handled in general, not a record of any actual incident involving any particular employer or employee.

RECORD RETENTION PERIODS AND EMPLOYEE ACCESS
Labor Code § 6401.9(f) sets specific minimum retention periods for several categories of records, longer than the one-year periods this corpus's IIPP information sheet describes for the general IIPP's inspection and training records under 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 3203(b). Subdivision (f)(1) provides that 'Records of workplace violence hazard identification, evaluation, and correction shall be created and maintained for a minimum of five years.' Subdivision (f)(3) separately provides that 'Violent incident logs required by subdivision (d) shall be maintained for a minimum of five years.' Subdivision (f)(6) then gives employees and their representatives a right to see certain of these records: 'All records required by paragraphs (1) to (3), inclusive, shall be made available to employees and their representatives, upon request and without cost, for examination and copying within 15 calendar days of a request.'

[Verified — checked 2026-09-02]
  "Records of workplace violence hazard identification, evaluation, and correction shall be created and maintained for a minimum of five years."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 6401.9 (California Legislative Information text), Lab. Code § 6401.9, subd. (f)(1) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=6401.9.)
  "Violent incident logs required by subdivision (d) shall be maintained for a minimum of five years."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 6401.9 (California Legislative Information text), Lab. Code § 6401.9, subd. (f)(3) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=6401.9.)
  "All records required by paragraphs (1) to (3), inclusive, shall be made available to employees and their representatives, upon request and without cost, for examination and copying within 15 calendar days of a request."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 6401.9 (California Legislative Information text), Lab. Code § 6401.9, subd. (f)(6) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=6401.9.)
  Known gap: This clause quotes only three of the six paragraphs of subdivision (f) — the hazard-record and log retention periods in (f)(1) and (f)(3), and the employee-access right in (f)(6) — and does not quote or fully summarize (f)(2) (one-year training-record retention), (f)(4) (five-year retention for incident investigation records, with a restriction on retaining 'medical information'), or (f)(5) (division access to records on request). All three quotations are drawn from the same enacted statute, Labor Code § 6401.9 — paragraphs of a single subdivision, (f) — not independent sources from one another; this document's only independent source is § 6401.9 itself, fetched twice from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov using two distinct request methods and confirmed byte-identical (after whitespace normalization) before any of its text was treated as verified. The 15-calendar-day access deadline stated here for records under paragraphs (1) through (3) of subdivision (f) is a different number and a different unit (calendar days, not business days) from the five-business-day access deadline this corpus's IIPP information sheet describes for the separate written IIPP itself under 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 3203(a)(8)(B)(1); the two access rights are not the same requirement and should not be conflated. This is a description of what the statute requires in general, not a record of any request made by or to any particular employer or employee.

ENFORCEMENT AND THE JULY 1, 2024 EFFECTIVE DATE
Labor Code § 6401.9(g) states how the section is enforced: 'The division shall enforce this section by the issuance of a citation alleging a violation of this section and a notice of civil penalty in a manner consistent with Section 6317.' The statute does not itself state a specific penalty amount in the text quoted here; it ties enforcement to the citation-and-penalty framework of a separate statute, Labor Code § 6317, which this clause does not independently verify or quote. On timing, subdivision (i) fixes when most of the section's substantive requirements took effect: 'Subdivisions (b) to (g), inclusive, shall be operative on and after July 1, 2024.' The statute was added by Stats. 2023, Ch. 289, § 4 (Senate Bill 553), with an original effective date of January 1, 2024, but subdivision (i) delays the operative date of subdivisions (b) through (g) — including the applicability rule, the plan requirement, the log requirement, training, and recordkeeping addressed in this information sheet's other clauses — to July 1, 2024.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-02]
  "The division shall enforce this section by the issuance of a citation alleging a violation of this section and a notice of civil penalty in a manner consistent with Section 6317."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 6401.9 (California Legislative Information text), Lab. Code § 6401.9, subd. (g) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=6401.9.)
  "Subdivisions (b) to (g), inclusive, shall be operative on and after July 1, 2024."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 6401.9 (California Legislative Information text), Lab. Code § 6401.9, subd. (i) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=6401.9.)
  Known gap: This clause does not independently fetch or verify Labor Code § 6317, the general citation-and-civil-penalty statute that § 6401.9(g) cross-references by section number only; no penalty amount or citation classification is stated or implied here beyond that cross-reference. Both quotations are drawn from the same enacted statute, Labor Code § 6401.9 — subdivisions (g) and (i) of one section — not independent sources from one another; this document's only independent source is § 6401.9 itself, fetched twice from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov using two distinct request methods and confirmed byte-identical (after whitespace normalization) before any of its text was treated as verified. Subdivision (i)'s text applies the July 1, 2024 operative date to subdivisions (b) through (g); it does not, on its own quoted terms, state an operative date for subdivision (a) (the definitions) or subdivision (h) (the division's and standards board's own deadlines to propose and adopt further standards), and this clause does not speculate about those subdivisions' effective dates beyond what subdivision (i)'s text itself says.

expectedJSON.body: Labor Code § 6401.9(c)(2) states that '[t]he plan shall include all of the following:' and then enumerates thirteen lettered elements, subparagraphs (A) through (M). This clause quotes a selection of those elements rather than all thirteen. Subparagraph (A) requires 'Names or job titles of the persons responsible for implementing the plan. If there are multiple persons responsible for the plan, their roles shall be clearly described.' Subparagraph (D) requires 'Effective procedures for the employer to accept and respond to reports of workplace violence, and to prohibit retaliation against an employee who makes such a report.' Subparagraph (I) requires 'Procedures to identify and evaluate workplace violence hazards, including, but not limited to, scheduled periodic inspections to identify unsafe conditions and work practices and employee reports and concerns. Inspections shall be conducted when the plan is first established, after each workplace violence incident, and whenever the employer is made aware of a new or previously unrecognized hazard.' Subparagraph (J) requires 'Procedures to correct workplace violence hazards identified and evaluated in subparagraph (I) in a timely manner consistent with paragraph (6) of subdivision (a) of Section 3203 of Title 8 of the California Code of Regulations.'

expectedJSON.body: Labor Code § 6401.9(e)(1) states the general training duty: 'The employer shall provide effective training to employees, as specified in paragraphs (2) and (3).' Subdivision (e)(2) then fixes the timing of the main round of training: 'The employer shall provide employees with initial training when the plan is first established, and annually thereafter, on all of the following:' — followed by six lettered topics the statute requires that training to cover, including the employer's plan itself, the definitions and requirements of the section, how to report incidents without fear of reprisal, and the job-specific hazards and corrective measures relevant to the employees being trained. Subdivision (e)(3) then adds a second, event-triggered training duty distinct from the annual cycle: 'Additional training shall be provided when a new or previously unrecognized workplace violence hazard has been identified and when changes are made to the plan. The additional training may be limited to addressing the new workplace violence hazard or changes to the plan.'

expectedJSON.body: Labor Code § 6401.9(d)(1)(A) states a duty distinct from the plan itself: 'The employer shall record information in a violent incident log for every workplace violence incident.' The statute separately protects the privacy of the people involved: subdivision (d)(1)(B) requires that 'The employer shall omit any element of personal identifying information sufficient to allow identification of any person involved in a violent incident, such as the person's name, address, electronic mail address, telephone number, social security number, or other information that, alone or in combination with other publicly available information, reveals the person's identity.' Subdivision (d)(2) then lists categories of information the log must include for each incident — such as the date, time, and location of the incident, the type of workplace violence involved, a description of the incident, and a classification of who committed it and the circumstances — which are not separately quoted in this clause.

Code Regs. § 3203(b). Subdivision (f)(1) provides that 'Records of workplace violence hazard identification, evaluation, and correction shall be created and maintained for a minimum of five years.' Subdivision (f)(3) separately provides that 'Violent incident logs required by subdivision (d) shall be maintained for a minimum of five years.' expectedJSON.body: Labor Code § 6401.9(g) states how the section is enforced: 'The division shall enforce this section by the issuance of a citation alleging a violation of this section and a notice of civil penalty in a manner consistent with Section 6317.' The statute does not itself state a specific penalty amount in the text quoted here; it ties enforcement to the citation-and-penalty framework of a separate statute, Labor Code § 6317, which this clause does not independently verify or quote. On timing, subdivision (i) fixes when most of the section's substantive requirements took effect: 'Subdivisions (b) to (g), inclusive, shall be operative on and after July 1, 2024.' The statute was added by Stats. 2023, Ch. 289, § 4 (Senate Bill 553), with an original effective date of January 1, 2024, but subdivision (i) delays the operative date of subdivisions (b) through (g) — including the applicability rule, the plan requirement, the log requirement, training, and recordkeeping addressed in this information sheet's other clauses — to July 1, 2024.
